verdict_summary.fp_grouping: 7 alerts sit on the framework's intentional, documented unsafe command/code-execution tool surfaces (ShellTool/BashProcess subprocess shell chain: bash.py:73/77/102 + shell/tool.py:69; PythonREPL exec chain: python.py:19 + tools/python/tool.py:58; PythonAstREPLTool: tools/python/tool.py:108)

cross_alert_observations: All 8 alerts share one entry edge: the AgentAction.tool_input attribute read at agents/agent.py:822 (src-r004) inside ExceptionTool().run(output.tool_input, ...) of the OutputParserException handler, propagated by the src-r057 fan-out summary (BaseTool.run tool_input -> every BaseTool subclass _run arg-1 param). ExceptionTool._run (agent.py:601-610) only echoes its input; the runtime-real dispatch to these tools is agent.py:850-851 (tool.run(agent_action.tool_input) with a dict-lookup receiver that static analysis cannot resolve). So every rendered codeFlow's first hop is a summary artifact, while the analogous genuine dispatch edge exists in source.

The alerts form 4 chains, each anchored by the same source site: (a) JIRA: jira/tool.py:51 -> jira.py:196/204/190 -> exec jira.py:192 [alert 3, REAL VULNERABILITY]; (b) Shell: shell/tool.py:69 -> bash.py:61 -> 73 -> 77 (subprocess.run shell=True) and persistent variant 97 -> 102 (sendline) [alerts 0/1/2/7]; (c) PythonREPL: tools/python/tool.py:58 -> python.py:14 -> 19 (exec) [alerts 4/5]; (d) PythonAstREPL: tools/python/tool.py:108 only [alert 6] — its deeper exec/eval (lines 117/123/130) is still unreachable due to the ast.parse/ast.unparse library barrier.

Within each chain the wrapper-param alerts are path prefixes of the argument-flow alerts (bash.py:73 is one hop short of bash.py:77; tools/python/tool.py:58 one hop short of python.py:19; shell/tool.py:69 three hops short of bash.py:77). They are redundant with, not independent of, the deeper alerts.

bash.py:102 (persistent sendline) additionally requires BashProcess(persistent=True); ShellTool's default factory constructs BashProcess(return_err_output=True) with persistent defaulting to False, so this branch needs explicit developer configuration.
The JIRA chain is qualitatively different from the other three: it is the only one whose sink executes input that the tool's declared function does not require to be code. See alert 3 rationale.

alerts.codeflow_verdict: The most complete path in this run: from jira.py:196 onward every step is genuine native dataflow (mode dispatch at :203-204 -> other param at :190 -> f-string interpolation at :192). The only summary edges are the entry fan-out (822 -> JiraAction._run) and the patched JiraAction -> JiraAPIWrapper.run hop. The entry site shown (822, ExceptionTool branch) is an artifact, but the real dispatch (agent.py:850-851, LLM selecting the 'Catch all Jira API call' tool) is verified reachable in source: JiraAPIWrapper.operations registers mode 'other' (jira.py:43), JiraToolkit.from_jira_api_wrapper instantiates a JiraAction per operation including mode='other' (toolkit.py:17-27), and initialize_agent exposes toolkit.get_tools() to the agent (documented usage in tools/jira/tool.py:13-29).

rationale.q1_source_attacker_influenced: Yes under the prompt-injection threat model: tool_input comes from the LLM parsing (AgentOutputParser.parse), and prompts embed user/external content. The JIRA catch-all prompt even instructs the LLM to supply 'a line of python code' (prompt.py JIRA_CATCH_ALL_PROMPT), so the code reaching exec is LLM-authored text influenced by the user's task and any injected content.
rationale.q2_llm_output_influences_tool_args: Yes — JiraAction._run receives the agent-dispatched instructions verbatim and forwards them as the `query` of api_wrapper.run('other', query).
rationale.q3_source_reaches_exec_sink: Yes — the chain agent dispatch -> JiraAction._run(instructions) -> JiraAPIWrapper.run(mode='other', query) -> other(query) -> exec(f"result = {query}") is fully present in source and reachable whenever the agent picks the 'other'-mode Jira tool (registered by default from JiraAPIWrapper.operations).
rationale.q4_propagation_evidence: Strong: every hop has direct source evidence (jira/tool.py:49-55; jira.py:196-204 mode dispatch; jira.py:190-194 exec). The only modeled (non-native) edges are the virtual-dispatch fan-out and the JiraAction -> api_wrapper pydantic Field call, both backed by real call sites.
rationale.q5_sink_executes_commands: Yes — builtin exec of an f-string that embeds the raw input: arbitrary Python code execution, not merely shell argument injection.
rationale.q6_command_string_untrusted: Yes — the executed code string is exactly the attacker-influenceable tool input; nothing is parsed, filtered, or restricted before interpolation.
rationale.q7_validation_or_blockers: None — other() does no validation; the mode dispatch only routes; JiraAction adds no checks; BaseTool._parse_input is type-validation only (x-r003).
rationale.q8_framework_provided_feature: No — this is the discriminator vs. the other 7 alerts. The 'other' mode is registered as a 'Catch all Jira API call' whose declared purpose is invoking atlassian-python-api Jira functions; executing arbitrary Python via exec is not the tool's declared function (contrast: every sibling mode — jql/get_projects/create_issue/create_page — parses structured input rather than evaluating it). Code execution here is an implementation artifact, not an offered capability, and it is not documented as an unsafe-by-design feature the way ShellTool/PythonREPL are (no warning, no 'use at your own risk').
rationale.q9_codeflow_real_path: Substantially yes: sink-side steps (jira.py:196 -> 204 -> 190 -> 192) are genuine native flow; the entry hop (822) is the fan-out artifact, with the real entry (850-851) verified in source but not statically resolved.
rationale.q10_overapproximation_fp: The entry edge is over-approximated, but the semantic chain is real end-to-end; no over-approximation is needed for the hop that matters (mode='other' dispatch -> exec).

alerts.notes: Highest-severity finding of the run: arbitrary code execution (exec of raw interpolated input) reachable from agent-dispatched, attacker-influenceable input, on a code path whose declared function is API wrapping, not code execution.
